title: Group, set or hierarchy?
summary: Sort Driftlight requests into group, set, hierarchy, bin or parameter, then see what each one builds and how to create it.
intro: Each card is a request from a Driftlight analyst. Decide which tool it calls for: a group, a set, a hierarchy, a bin or a parameter. After you answer, you see a sketch of what it builds and how to create it. The sandbox can't build these yet, so the sketches are schematic.

copy.s1: Combine the spelling variants Cologne and Köln into one city, so the board sees a single bar.
copy.s1Why: A group combines related members of a field into a single bigger member. Merging spellings is the classic case.
copy.s1How: Select the two headers or marks and click the group icon (a paperclip) on the tooltip, or right-click the field in the Data pane and choose Create > Group. Click Rename to give the group a better name than the default.
copy.s2: Marketing wants the top 20 titles by minutes, refreshed every week as viewing changes.
copy.s2Why: A top N by a measure that must follow the data is a dynamic set, defined on the Top tab. Every title is either In or Out of the set.
copy.s2How: Right-click the dimension in the Data pane and choose Create > Set, then use the Top tab. Because it is defined by a rule, its members change when the underlying data changes.
copy.s3: The catalogue team wants to start at Type, then click to see Genre, then Sub-Genre, only where they need detail.
copy.s3Why: Related dimensions stacked from general to detailed so the viewer can drill down and up are a hierarchy.
copy.s3How: In the Data pane, drag a field and drop it on top of another field, then name the hierarchy and drag more fields in, from general to detailed. In the view, click the + or - icon on the hierarchy field to drill down or up.
copy.s4: Show how long sessions typically last by counting sessions in equal ranges of minutes watched.
copy.s4Why: Bins cut a continuous measure into equal ranges and create a new dimension, which is the basis of a histogram.
copy.s4How: Right-click the measure in the Data pane and choose Create > Bins, then enter the size of bins. Or select the measure and pick histogram in Show Me. The measure then aggregates as a count instead of a sum.
copy.s5: The head of content wants one control that switches every chart between minutes and number of sessions.
copy.s5Why: A parameter is a single value the viewer can change that a calculation can use in place of a constant. Letting the viewer swap measures is a standard use.
copy.s5How: Open the menu at the top of the Data pane and choose Create Parameter, give it a List of allowable values, then right-click it and choose Show Parameter. A calculation has to use it, or the control does nothing.
copy.s6: The content team wants Scripted and Unscripted genres, with every remaining genre lumped into one bucket.
copy.s6Why: Bundling members into broader categories is a group. The Include 'Other' option lumps the non-grouped members together.
copy.s6How: Right-click the field in the Data pane, choose Create > Group, and select the members to combine. In the Edit Group dialog, select Include 'Other' to put all the remaining members in an Other group.
copy.s7: An analyst selects five title marks in a bar chart and wants to keep exactly those titles as a subset, even when the data changes.
copy.s7Why: A subset picked by hand from marks is a fixed set: its members do not change, even if the underlying data changes.
copy.s7How: Right-click the selected marks and choose Create Set. Choose Exclude these members instead if the set should hold everything except the selection.
copy.s8: Let viewers type their own target and see a reference line move to it.
copy.s8Why: A parameter can replace the constant in a reference line, and it holds one value that the viewer supplies.
copy.s8How: Create the parameter from the Data pane menu, choose its data type and allowable values, show it with Show Parameter, then use it as the Constant value of the reference line.
copy.s9: Show the top titles in one colour and every other title in a second colour, to compare the two.
copy.s9Why: A set divides members into In and Out, and putting it on Color with In/Out shown gives exactly two categories.
copy.s9How: Build the set, then right-click it and choose Show In/Out of Set, and place it on Color. A set can also be shown as its members.
copy.viewGroup: In the view: separate members merge into one header or mark. In the Data pane: a new group field with a paperclip icon.
copy.viewSet: In the view: every member is In or Out of the set. In the Data pane: a new set field.
copy.viewHierarchy: In the view: clicking + on the hierarchy field adds the next field as nested headers. In the Data pane: a hierarchy folder of fields, general to detailed.
copy.viewBin: In the view: a histogram, one bar per range, counting records. In the Data pane: a new dimension of ranges, named like the measure with (bin).
copy.viewParameter: In the view: a control the viewer changes, holding one value. In the Data pane: a parameter, with nothing changing until a calculation, filter or reference line uses it.
copy.done: All scenarios answered. Use Start over to try them again.
